newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RANGERS ELIMINATE DEFENDING EASTERN CONFERENCE CHAMPIONS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RANGERS ELIMINATE DEFENDING EASTERN CONFERENCE CHAMPIONS.

text.p: Esa Tikkanen's second overtime goal of the playoffs, 12:08 into the extra session, gave the New York Rangers a 3-2 win over the Florida Panthers Friday that eliminated the defending Eastern Conference champions.
The Rangers claimed the best-of-seven series by four games to one, sweeping the last four after dropping the opener.

Brian Leetch started the climactic play in his own end and passed the puck to Mark Messier, who penetrated the Florida zone on the left side and sent a pass to Tikkanen, who was cutting through the slot from right to left.
Tikkanen fired a shot that deflected off the skate of Florida defenceman Terry Carkner and beat John Vanbiesbrouck to his glove side.
"It was 2-on-2, Mess passed the puck and I shot it, Carkner went down and then I saw the guys celebrating," said Tikkanen. "Everyone talked about how old we are, but we're looking like young kids."
Messier scored the other two goals for New York, who never trailed. Mike Richter stopped 38 shots for the Rangers, who won four straight games after a 3-0 loss in Game One.

Florida coach Doug Mac Lean said: "I don't think the Rangers played that much better than us, but their big players Wayne Gretzky, Mark Messier and Esa Tikkanen came up big for them, getting big goals at key times.
"Give them credit, their big guys came up big. They were criticised they were too old, but they came up real big."

Mike Hough and Ray Sheppard tallied for the Panthers, who last year eliminated Boston, Philadelphia and Pittsburgh in the Eastern Conference before being swept by the Colorado Avalanche in the Stanley Cup finals.
Vanbiesbrouck made 30 saves for Florida.
Gretzky, who scored a hat trick in leading the Rangers to a 3-2 win in Game Four, said: "Wednesday was my night, tonight Mark (Messier) had his game face on. It was his night."

In Buffalo, Daniel Alfredsson scored two goals and Ron Tugnutt stopped 24 shots as the seventh-seeded Ottawa Senators pushed the Buffalo Sabres to the brink of elimination with a 4-1 victory in Game Five of their Eastern Conference series.
Randy Cunneyworth and Shawn McEachern also scored for the Senators, who lead the best-of-seven series three games to two and can advance with a win at Ottawa in Game Six on Sunday.
Donald Audette accounted for the Buffalo offence with a goal in the third period. The Sabres again played without starting goaltender Dominik Hasek, out with a sprained knee.
Buffalo general manager John Muckler ruled out Hasek for Game Six before Friday night's game, but said he may be available for a possible Game Seven.

In Detroit, Brendan Shanahan collected a goal and two assists and Steve Yzerman and Larry Murphy each added a goal and an assist as the Detroit Red Wings beat the St. Louis Blues 5-2 to move within one win of the Western Conference semifinals.
Vyacheslav Kozlov and Darren McCarty scored second-period goals for the Red Wings, who can clinch the series with a victory in Game Six in St. Louis Sunday afternoon.
Detroit matched their goals output in the four previous games of the series.
"I don't think we played poorly the first four games, Detroit coach Scotty Bowman said. "But it's not much fun when you're not scoring.
"Their guy (goalie Grant Fuhr) had a 95 save percentage, so we were getting the chances, we just weren't getting them in. Sometimes all you need is a good bounce and we got that with Yzerman's goal."

Jim Campbell recorded his first goal of the series, a power-play tally with 7:46 left in the second, drawing the Blues within 3-2. But Shanahan's second goal of the series just 61 seconds later restored the two-goal edge.
"It was nice to see some goals, that will help everyone's confidence," Murphy said. "But you have to be realistic, maybe we'll only score one next game and we'll have to battle for that to stand up."

In Dallas, Ryan Smyth scored the game's only goal 22 seconds into the second overtime and Curtis Joseph stopped 43 shots as the Edmonton Oilers defeated the Dallas Stars 1-0 to take a 3-2 lead in their Western Conference playoff series.
It was the second overtime win of the series for the Oilers, who rallied from a 3-0 deficit and beat Dallas 4-3 in overtime in Game Three last Sunday.
Game Six is Sunday afternoon at Edmonton.

The Stars outshot the Oilers 35-14 through regulation but were unable to beat Joseph. Edmonton managed just one shot in the first 17 minutes of the third period and finished the period with only three shots.
